I'm 50 this year, and I've been farming these 7 mu in Quzhou for 30 years. My wife and I manage the farm together. We both pick up off-farm construction work when it's available—our son works in Shijiazhuang and our daughter is in Handan, so they send some money back, but the farm is still our base. I finished middle school, so I can read the fertilizer bags and understand what the extension agent says, but honestly, most of what I know comes from doing this for three decades and watching what works for my neighbors.

This year I'm keeping 3 mu in cotton and 4 mu in single-crop maize. I thought about planting more cotton because the lint price was decent last year—about 7.5 yuan per jin—but cotton is just too much work for the two of us, especially the picking in autumn. Maize is easier. The combine harvester can handle maize in a few hours, but cotton has to be picked by hand four or five times. Last year I tried 4 mu of cotton and I was worn out by October, so I'm cutting back to 3 mu this year.

For the cotton, I'm planting right now in late April. I'm buying hybrid seed again—about 45 yuan per mu. I don't save my own cotton seed because the hybrid varieties are much better. The soil on my cotton plot is decent, a bit sandy. I usually put down compound fertilizer as base, about 30 kg per mu, and then topdress with urea at flowering—around 20 kg per mu. That works out to roughly 15 kg of nitrogen per mu total. The extension agent always says I should do 18 kg, but 15 kg has been enough for me, and I don't want to waste money. If I put too much nitrogen, the cotton grows too tall and falls over anyway. I'll irrigate three times: once after planting if the weather stays dry, once at flowering in July, and once when the bolls are setting in August. Each time costs about 40 yuan per mu for electricity to pump the well water. For chemicals, I definitely need herbicide—I'll spray once before planting and maybe cultivate once more by hand. For insects, bollworm is the main problem, so I'll spray insecticide two or three times starting in July. I expect about 240 kg of lint per mu if the weather cooperates. That was about my average the last few years.

For the maize, I'll wait until early May to plant. I learned years ago that if you plant too early and get a cold snap, the seedlings suffer. The soil needs to warm up. I'm using hybrid seed too, about 55 yuan per mu. For fertilizer, I'll put compound fertilizer in the furrow at planting, about 25 kg per mu, then topdress with urea at the jointing stage in July—about 20 kg per mu. That's around 16 kg of nitrogen per mu in total. The maize plot had wheat on it two years ago, so the soil still has some fertility. I might irrigate twice—once at jointing and once at tasseling—but if July and August bring good rains, maybe just once. Water costs add up, and maize can handle a bit of drought better than cotton. I'll spray herbicide once after emergence to control weeds. For harvest, I'll hire the combine—about 50 yuan per mu. Much faster than doing it by hand, and by late September I need to free up time for cotton picking.

Labor is always tight. My wife and I will do most of the work ourselves—probably about 25 days total on the cotton and 12 days on the maize through the season. But during cotton picking in September and October, if we're both busy with off-farm jobs, I might hire a local woman for 2 or 3 days to help pick. That costs about 150 yuan per day, but it's better than losing cotton to weather.

I'm budgeting about 4,000 yuan total for seeds, fertilizer, pesticides, irrigation, and hired help. I have about 5,000 yuan set aside for farming this year, so that leaves me a buffer. I never spend every yuan on the farm—you need cash in hand for emergencies. A bad year hurts more than a good year helps, so I stick with what I know works.
